text: What is the Spring Boot annotation to mark the main application class?
explanation:
@SpringBootApplication is correct because it combines @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan, so it is the standard annotation on the main Spring Boot class.

Example: a typical entry point looks like this:

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;

@SpringBootApplication
public class DemoApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args);
    }
}

text: Which dependency is typically used for building REST APIs in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-web is correct because it pulls in the dependencies needed for REST controllers, JSON serialization, and the embedded servlet container used by most Spring Boot APIs.

Example: after adding that starter, you can expose an endpoint like this:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/users")
public class UserController {
    @GetMapping
    public List<String> findAll() {
        return List.of("Alice", "Bob");
    }
}

text: In Spring, which annotation is used for constructor-based dependency injection?
explanation:
@Autowired is correct because Spring uses it to inject a matching bean, and it is commonly seen on constructors when wiring required dependencies.

Example:

@Service
public class OrderService {
    private final PaymentService paymentService;

    @Autowired
    public OrderService(PaymentService paymentService) {
        this.paymentService = paymentService;
    }
}

text: Which file defines Spring profiles and properties for different environments?
explanation:
application.properties is correct because that file is the conventional place to keep Spring Boot configuration such as ports, profiles, logging, and datasource properties.

Example:

server.port=8081
spring.profiles.active=dev
logging.level.org.springframework.web=DEBUG

text: Which Spring module provides integration with relational databases using repositories?
explanation:
Spring Data JPA is correct because it provides repository abstractions and JPA integration so relational data access can be written with much less boilerplate.

Example:

@Entity
public class Customer {
    @Id
    private Long id;
}

public interface CustomerRepository extends JpaRepository<Customer, Long> {
}

text: In Spring Data JPA, which annotation marks the primary key of an entity?
explanation:
@Id is correct because JPA uses @Id to mark the field or property that represents the primary key of an entity.

Example:

@Entity
public class Product {
    @Id
    private Long id;
    private String name;
}

text: What is the default port for a Spring Boot application?
explanation:
8080 is correct because Spring Boot listens on port 8080 by default unless you override server.port.

Example: if you run the app locally with default settings, you usually open http://localhost:8080.

text: Which annotation maps an HTTP GET request to a controller method?
explanation:
@GetMapping is correct because it is the shortcut annotation for mapping HTTP GET requests to a controller method.

Example:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/books")
public class BookController {
    @GetMapping
    public List<String> list() {
        return List.of("Spring in Action");
    }
}

text: Which Spring Boot starter adds actuator endpoints for monitoring?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-actuator is correct because it adds production-ready endpoints for health checks, metrics, and application diagnostics.

Example: after adding the starter, endpoints such as /actuator/health can be exposed for monitoring.

text: Which Spring annotation secures methods or classes?
explanation:
@PreAuthorize is correct because it is a Spring Security annotation used to enforce authorization rules before a method is executed.

Example:

@Service
public class AdminService {
    @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
    public void deleteUser(Long id) {
    }
}

text: Which Spring annotation maps a class to a REST controller?
explanation:
@RestController is correct because it combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, which makes it the standard choice for JSON-based APIs.

Example:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/health")
public class HealthController {
    @GetMapping
    public Map<String, String> health() {
        return Map.of("status", "UP");
    }
}

text: Which Spring component scans for annotated classes during startup?
explanation:
Component scanning is correct because Spring uses component scanning to discover classes annotated with stereotypes such as @Component, @Service, and @Repository.

Example:

@Component
public class AuditFormatter {
}

text: In Spring Boot, which file enables configuring logging levels?
explanation:
application.properties is correct because that file is the conventional place to keep Spring Boot configuration such as ports, profiles, logging, and datasource properties.

Example:

server.port=8081
spring.profiles.active=dev
logging.level.org.springframework.web=DEBUG

text: Which annotation binds external configuration values to a POJO in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@ConfigurationProperties is correct because Spring Boot uses @ConfigurationProperties when you want to map a whole group of related properties into a strongly typed class instead of reading individual keys one by one.

Example:

@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "app.mail")
public class MailProperties {
    private String host;
    private int port;
}

text: Which dependency is commonly added for validating request payloads in a Spring Boot REST API?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-validation is correct because Validation in Boot is usually enabled through spring-boot-starter-validation, which brings in Jakarta Bean Validation and lets annotations like @NotBlank work on DTOs.

Example:

public record UserRequest(@NotBlank String name, @Email String email) { }

text: Which annotation triggers validation on a controller method parameter in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@Valid is correct because Use @Valid on request bodies or nested objects so Spring validates the payload before your controller logic runs.

Example:

@PostMapping
public User create(@Valid @RequestBody UserRequest request) {
    return service.create(request);
}

text: Which file is loaded automatically for profile-specific configuration in the dev profile?
explanation:
application-dev.properties is correct because Spring Boot automatically looks for profile-specific files like application-dev.properties when the dev profile is active.

Example:

spring.profiles.active=dev

text: Which annotation marks a method to run after the Spring Boot application context starts?
explanation:
@EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent.class) is correct because If logic must run only after the full application is ready, listening for ApplicationReadyEvent is safer than doing it too early.

Example:

@Component
public class StartupTasks {
    @EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent.class)
    public void warmUp() { }
}

text: What is the usual superclass for custom runtime errors returned by a Spring Boot API?
explanation:
RuntimeException is correct because Business exceptions in Spring Boot commonly extend RuntimeException so they can bubble up to a global exception handler.

Example:

public class OrderNotFoundException extends RuntimeException {
    public OrderNotFoundException(Long id) {
        super("Order not found: " + id);
    }
}

text: Which annotation is typically used to centralize exception handling across controllers?
explanation:
@RestControllerAdvice is correct because A @RestControllerAdvice class can convert many exceptions into consistent JSON responses for the whole API.

Example:

@RestControllerAdvice
public class ApiExceptionHandler {
    @ExceptionHandler(OrderNotFoundException.class)
    ResponseEntity<String> handle(OrderNotFoundException ex) {
        return ResponseEntity.status(404).body(ex.getMessage());
    }
}

text: Which embedded server is the default for spring-boot-starter-web?
explanation:
Tomcat is correct because The standard web starter brings embedded Tomcat by default, which means most Boot MVC apps run without installing a separate server.

Example:

Example: running the JAR starts Tomcat automatically on port 8080 unless you change it.

text: Which annotation enables asynchronous method execution in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@EnableAsync is correct because Boot supports async methods when async processing is enabled, usually with @EnableAsync on a configuration class.

Example:

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableAsync
public class DemoApplication { }

text: Which annotation marks a method for asynchronous execution?
explanation:
@Async is correct because A method annotated with @Async can run on a task executor so the caller does not block waiting for completion.

Example:

@Service
public class EmailService {
    @Async
    public CompletableFuture<Void> sendWelcomeMail() {
        return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(null);
    }
}

text: Which annotation is used to cache the result of a method in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@Cacheable is correct because Use @Cacheable when repeated calls with the same inputs should reuse a cached result instead of recalculating it.

Example:

@Cacheable("products")
public Product findById(Long id) {
    return repository.findById(id).orElseThrow();
}

text: Which annotation turns on Spring cache support?
explanation:
@EnableCaching is correct because Caching annotations do not take effect until cache support is enabled, typically with @EnableCaching.

Example:

@Configuration
@EnableCaching
class CacheConfig { }

text: Which actuator endpoint is commonly used by load balancers to check application health?
explanation:
/actuator/health is correct because The health endpoint is designed for readiness and liveness style checks because it summarizes whether the app and its dependencies are healthy.

Example:

Example: Kubernetes or a load balancer can probe /actuator/health.

text: Which configuration property changes the HTTP port of a Spring Boot app?
explanation:
server.port is correct because Boot exposes the listening port through the server.port property, so you can move the app off the default 8080 easily.

Example:

server.port=9090

text: Which configuration property sets the application context path in Spring Boot?
explanation:
server.servlet.context-path is correct because If all endpoints should sit under a prefix such as /quiz, Boot uses server.servlet.context-path.

Example:

server.servlet.context-path=/quiz

text: Which annotation injects a property value directly into a field or constructor parameter?
explanation:
@Value is correct because Use @Value for simple one-off property injection when you do not need a full configuration properties class.

Example:

@Value("${app.title}")
private String title;

text: Which starter is commonly used when adding unit and integration testing support to Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-test is correct because The Boot test starter bundles common testing tools such as JUnit, AssertJ, Mockito, and Spring Test in one dependency.

Example:

<dependency>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>

text: Which annotation loads the full Spring Boot application context in a test?
explanation:
@SpringBootTest is correct because Use @SpringBootTest when the test should start the real Spring Boot context and wire beans as the application would.

Example:

@SpringBootTest
class OrderServiceTest { }

text: Which Spring test utility is commonly used to test MVC controllers without starting a real server?
explanation:
MockMvc is correct because With MockMvc, you can test controller routes, status codes, and JSON payloads at the MVC layer without deploying the app.

Example:

mockMvc.perform(get("/api/books"))
       .andExpect(status().isOk());

text: Which annotation narrows a Spring Boot test to MVC components only?
explanation:
@WebMvcTest is correct because A slice test with @WebMvcTest loads controllers and MVC infrastructure, which keeps controller tests fast and focused.

Example:

@WebMvcTest(BookController.class)
class BookControllerTest { }

text: Which annotation is commonly used for JPA repository tests with an embedded database?
explanation:
@DataJpaTest is correct because The @DataJpaTest slice configures repositories, entities, and transaction rollback behavior for focused persistence testing.

Example:

@DataJpaTest
class CustomerRepositoryTest { }

text: Which property is often used to configure the JDBC URL in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring.datasource.url is correct because The datasource URL tells Spring Boot how to connect to the database, including host, port, and database name.

Example:

spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/appdb

text: Which property defines the Hibernate DDL strategy in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto is correct because This property controls whether Hibernate creates, updates, validates, or leaves the schema alone at startup.

Example:

spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update

text: Which starter is commonly used to send emails from a Spring Boot application?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-mail is correct because The mail starter adds the JavaMail support typically needed for password resets, notifications, and alerts.

Example:

spring.mail.host=smtp.example.com

text: Which actuator endpoint shows arbitrary application metadata like version and build info?
explanation:
/actuator/info is correct because The info endpoint is intended for metadata such as app version, commit ID, or environment details that you want to expose safely.

Example:

Example: you can publish the build version so support teams know what is deployed.

text: Which property activates a profile directly from configuration?
explanation:
spring.profiles.active is correct because Boot selects profile-specific beans and properties based on spring.profiles.active.

Example:

spring.profiles.active=prod

text: Which annotation loads a bean only when a specific profile is active?
explanation:
@Profile is correct because Use @Profile when a bean should exist only in environments like dev or prod.

Example:

@Bean
@Profile("dev")
CommandLineRunner seedData() {
    return args -> { };
}

text: Which class is most commonly used to build a JAR from a Spring Boot application?
explanation:
SpringApplication is correct because Although packaging is handled by the build tool, SpringApplication is the runtime entry point that boots the packaged application.

Example:

SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args);

text: Which Maven plugin is commonly used to package and run Spring Boot apps?
explanation:
spring-boot-maven-plugin is correct because The Boot Maven plugin helps repackage the app as an executable JAR and supports commands like spring-boot:run.

Example:

<plugin>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
</plugin>

text: Which Gradle plugin is typically applied in a Spring Boot project?
explanation:
org.springframework.boot is correct because In Gradle builds, the org.springframework.boot plugin adds Boot packaging and dependency management conveniences.

Example:

plugins {
    id "org.springframework.boot" version "3.3.0"
}

text: Which annotation exposes a Java method as a Spring bean inside a configuration class?
explanation:
@Bean is correct because When an object should be created with custom logic, a @Bean method lets Spring manage it in the application context.

Example:

@Configuration
class AppConfig {
    @Bean
    Clock clock() {
        return Clock.systemUTC();
    }
}

text: Which annotation marks a class as a source of bean definitions?
explanation:
@Configuration is correct because A class annotated with @Configuration is intended to declare bean methods and application wiring.

Example:

@Configuration
class SecurityConfig { }

text: Which annotation maps a JSON request body to a Java object in a controller method?
explanation:
@RequestBody is correct because In REST controllers, @RequestBody tells Spring to deserialize the incoming JSON into your DTO or entity object.

Example:

@PostMapping
public Order create(@RequestBody OrderRequest request) {
    return service.create(request);
}

text: Which annotation extracts a value from the URL path in a Spring Boot controller?
explanation:
@PathVariable is correct because Use @PathVariable when the route itself contains the value you need, such as an order ID.

Example:

@GetMapping("/{id}")
public Order find(@PathVariable Long id) {
    return service.find(id);
}

text: Which annotation reads a query parameter in a Spring Boot controller?
explanation:
@RequestParam is correct because Query-string values like ?page=2 are typically mapped with @RequestParam.

Example:

@GetMapping
public List<Order> list(@RequestParam int page) {
    return service.list(page);
}

text: Which annotation sets the base URL path for all handler methods in a controller?
explanation:
@RequestMapping is correct because Putting @RequestMapping on the class avoids repeating the same URL prefix on every endpoint method.

Example:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/orders")
class OrderController { }

text: Which Spring Boot feature automatically configures beans based on the classpath and properties?
explanation:
Auto-configuration is correct because Auto-configuration is one of Boot’s biggest productivity features because it creates sensible defaults from the libraries you include.

Example:

Example: adding the web starter configures JSON converters and an embedded server automatically.

text: Which annotation excludes a specific auto-configuration class?
explanation:
@SpringBootApplication(exclude = ...) is correct because If one Boot auto-configuration is not wanted, you can exclude it explicitly on the main application annotation.

Example:

@SpringBootApplication(exclude = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class)
class DemoApplication { }

text: Which starter is commonly used to build reactive APIs in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-webflux is correct because Reactive HTTP applications in Boot usually start with spring-boot-starter-webflux rather than the MVC web starter.

Example:

@GetMapping("/ticks")
public Flux<Long> ticks() {
    return Flux.interval(Duration.ofSeconds(1));
}

text: Which server is commonly used by default with Spring WebFlux applications?
explanation:
Netty is correct because WebFlux applications often run on Reactor Netty by default, which fits the reactive, non-blocking programming model.

Example:

Example: a WebFlux starter app usually starts with embedded Netty unless reconfigured.

text: Which annotation marks a component as part of the service layer?
explanation:
@Service is correct because While technically a specialization of @Component, @Service communicates intent and is the usual stereotype for business logic.

Example:

@Service
public class BillingService { }

text: Which annotation marks a persistence component such as a repository implementation?
explanation:
@Repository is correct because Use @Repository for data-access components so Spring can detect them and translate persistence exceptions.

Example:

@Repository
public class JdbcReportRepository { }

text: Which annotation marks a general-purpose Spring-managed class?
explanation:
@Component is correct because When a class does not clearly fit service, controller, or repository roles, @Component is the generic stereotype.

Example:

@Component
public class SlugGenerator { }

text: Which property controls log verbosity for a specific package in Spring Boot?
explanation:
logging.level. is correct because Per-package logging configuration lets you increase detail for one part of the app without flooding everything else.

Example:

logging.level.com.example.quiz=DEBUG

text: Which file format can Spring Boot use in addition to .properties for configuration?
explanation:
application.yml is correct because Boot supports YAML as a readable alternative to properties files, especially for nested configuration structures.

Example:

server:
  port: 8081

text: Which annotation binds a controller method to HTTP POST requests?
explanation:
@PostMapping is correct because Use @PostMapping for endpoints that create resources or accept submitted data via HTTP POST.

Example:

@PostMapping
public ResponseEntity<Order> create(@RequestBody OrderRequest request) {
    return ResponseEntity.ok(service.create(request));
}

text: Which annotation binds a controller method to HTTP PUT requests?
explanation:
@PutMapping is correct because A full resource update is commonly modeled as an HTTP PUT endpoint, mapped with @PutMapping.

Example:

@PutMapping("/{id}")
public Order update(@PathVariable Long id, @RequestBody OrderRequest request) {
    return service.update(id, request);
}

text: Which annotation binds a controller method to HTTP DELETE requests?
explanation:
@DeleteMapping is correct because Delete endpoints are conventionally implemented with @DeleteMapping so the route clearly matches the HTTP verb.

Example:

@DeleteMapping("/{id}")
public void delete(@PathVariable Long id) {
    service.delete(id);
}

text: Which annotation binds a controller method to HTTP PATCH requests?
explanation:
@PatchMapping is correct because A partial update is usually expressed with HTTP PATCH, which Spring maps neatly via @PatchMapping.

Example:

@PatchMapping("/{id}/status")
public Order updateStatus(@PathVariable Long id) {
    return service.advance(id);
}

text: Which annotation is commonly used to enable scheduling in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@EnableScheduling is correct because Scheduled jobs are turned on with @EnableScheduling, after which methods can use @Scheduled.

Example:

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableScheduling
class DemoApplication { }

text: Which annotation schedules a method to run at fixed intervals?
explanation:
@Scheduled is correct because The @Scheduled annotation is the standard way to run recurring background jobs in a Spring Boot app.

Example:

@Scheduled(fixedRate = 60000)
public void refreshCache() { }

text: Which property is often used to expose all actuator endpoints for local development?
explanation:
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=* is correct because For local debugging, developers sometimes expose all actuator web endpoints through the management exposure property.

Example:

management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=*

text: Which starter is commonly used to secure a Spring Boot application?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-security is correct because Security features such as authentication filters and authorization support usually begin with the security starter.

Example:

<artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>

text: Which bean type is commonly defined to customize HTTP security rules in modern Spring Boot?
explanation:
SecurityFilterChain is correct because Modern Spring Security configuration in Boot usually exposes a SecurityFilterChain bean instead of extending the older adapter class.

Example:

@Bean
SecurityFilterChain security(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    return http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth.anyRequest().authenticated()).build();
}

text: Which annotation enables method-level validation in a Spring service class?
explanation:
@Validated is correct because When method parameters on a bean should be validated, @Validated is commonly placed on the class.

Example:

@Service
@Validated
public class CouponService {
    public void apply(@NotBlank String code) { }
}

text: Which class is commonly returned to customize HTTP status and body in Spring Boot controllers?
explanation:
ResponseEntity is correct because Use ResponseEntity when you need explicit control over the status code, headers, and response body.

Example:

return ResponseEntity.status(201).body(order);

text: Which annotation customizes the HTTP status returned by a controller method?
explanation:
@ResponseStatus is correct because If an endpoint or exception should always map to a particular status, @ResponseStatus provides a clean declaration.

Example:

@ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
@PostMapping
public Order create(@RequestBody OrderRequest request) { ... }

text: Which Spring Boot property enables SQL logging for JPA?
explanation:
spring.jpa.show-sql is correct because Turning on SQL output is useful during development when you need to confirm what Hibernate is sending to the database.

Example:

spring.jpa.show-sql=true

text: Which annotation groups related REST endpoints in one class?
explanation:
@RestController is correct because A REST controller is the normal place to organize endpoints that belong to one resource area such as users, orders, or products.

Example:

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/products")
class ProductController { }

text: Which annotation injects a repository or service through the constructor without field injection?
explanation:
@Autowired is correct because Constructor injection is preferred for required dependencies, and Spring can wire them using @Autowired or implicitly with a single constructor.

Example:

public OrderController(OrderService orderService) {
    this.orderService = orderService;
}

text: Which annotation resolves ambiguity when multiple beans of the same type exist?
explanation:
@Qualifier is correct because When Spring finds several beans of the same type, @Qualifier lets you choose the intended one explicitly.

Example:

public ReportService(@Qualifier("pdfExporter") Exporter exporter) {
    this.exporter = exporter;
}

text: Which annotation marks one bean as the default choice when multiple candidates exist?
explanation:
@Primary is correct because Use @Primary when one bean should win by default during autowiring unless a qualifier says otherwise.

Example:

@Bean
@Primary
Clock utcClock() {
    return Clock.systemUTC();
}

text: Which Spring Boot feature allows externalized configuration through environment variables, files, and command-line args?
explanation:
Externalized configuration is correct because Externalized configuration is central to Boot because the same code can run in dev, test, and production with different settings.

Example:

Example: SERVER_PORT=9090 can override the configured port without changing code.

text: Which annotation is commonly used on the main class to scan components from its package and subpackages?
explanation:
@SpringBootApplication is correct because Because @SpringBootApplication includes component scanning, placing the main class in a root package helps discover controllers and services automatically.

Example:

Example: if the main class is in com.example.app, Boot scans subpackages below it.

text: Which interface is often implemented for startup logic that needs command-line arguments?
explanation:
CommandLineRunner is correct because A CommandLineRunner bean runs after the context is ready and receives any command-line arguments passed to the app.

Example:

@Bean
CommandLineRunner init() {
    return args -> System.out.println(Arrays.toString(args));
}

text: Which interface is similar to CommandLineRunner but receives arguments as ApplicationArguments?
explanation:
ApplicationRunner is correct because Use ApplicationRunner when you want a more structured view of startup arguments instead of a raw string array.

Example:

@Bean
ApplicationRunner run() {
    return args -> System.out.println(args.getOptionNames());
}

text: Which annotation is used to enable configuration properties scanning in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@ConfigurationPropertiesScan is correct because When configuration properties classes are not registered another way, Boot can discover them through @ConfigurationPropertiesScan.

Example:

@SpringBootApplication
@ConfigurationPropertiesScan
class DemoApplication { }

text: Which property controls multipart file upload size in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size is correct because File upload limits are configured through Boot’s multipart properties so uploads can be constrained without code changes.

Example:

spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size=10MB

text: Which annotation enables cross-origin requests on a Spring Boot controller or method?
explanation:
@CrossOrigin is correct because Use @CrossOrigin when a browser-based frontend on another origin must call your Boot API.

Example:

@CrossOrigin(origins = "http://localhost:4200")
@RestController
class QuizController { }

text: Which Spring Boot starter is typically used for WebSocket support?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-websocket is correct because WebSocket applications in Spring Boot usually begin with the dedicated websocket starter.

Example:

@EnableWebSocketMessageBroker
@Configuration
class WebSocketConfig { }

text: Which starter is commonly used for building SOAP web services in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-web-services is correct because SOAP-based integrations in Boot typically use the web services starter rather than the REST web starter alone.

Example:

Example: this starter is useful when integrating with legacy enterprise SOAP systems.

text: Which annotation maps HTTP headers to a controller method parameter?
explanation:
@RequestHeader is correct because When an endpoint needs values like authorization metadata or tenant IDs from headers, @RequestHeader is the usual choice.

Example:

@GetMapping
public String who(@RequestHeader("X-Tenant") String tenant) {
    return tenant;
}

text: Which annotation maps a cookie value to a controller method parameter?
explanation:
@CookieValue is correct because Use @CookieValue when the controller should read a cookie such as a session preference or tracking token.

Example:

public String theme(@CookieValue("theme") String theme) {
    return theme;
}

text: Which annotation is commonly used to serialize all return values in a controller as JSON?
explanation:
@RestController is correct because A @RestController returns data directly rather than resolving server-side views, which is why it is standard for APIs.

Example:

Example: returning a POJO from a @RestController method is automatically converted to JSON.

text: Which Spring Boot feature automatically serves static files from folders like /static or /public?
explanation:
Static resource auto-configuration is correct because Boot can serve CSS, JavaScript, and images automatically from conventional resource folders without extra controller code.

Example:

Example: a file in src/main/resources/static/app.js is served directly by the app.

text: Which annotation is commonly used to document APIs with springdoc OpenAPI controllers?
explanation:
@Operation is correct because When using springdoc, @Operation adds summary and description metadata for generated OpenAPI docs.

Example:

@Operation(summary = "Find user by id")
@GetMapping("/{id}")
public User find(@PathVariable Long id) { ... }

text: Which health group concept in Spring Boot actuator lets you separate readiness from liveness checks?
explanation:
Probes is correct because Actuator can expose liveness and readiness probes separately so orchestrators can make better traffic decisions.

Example:

Example: /actuator/health/liveness and /actuator/health/readiness.

text: Which annotation enables retry support when using Spring Retry with Spring Boot?
explanation:
@EnableRetry is correct because If you add Spring Retry, methods can use retry semantics once retry support is enabled with @EnableRetry.

Example:

@Configuration
@EnableRetry
class RetryConfig { }

text: Which annotation retries a method call when certain failures occur?
explanation:
@Retryable is correct because A @Retryable method is useful for transient failures such as temporary network or database connection problems.

Example:

@Retryable
public String fetchRemoteData() {
    return client.call();
}

text: Which annotation defines a fallback method for exhausted retries in Spring Retry?
explanation:
@Recover is correct because A recovery method gives your application a controlled fallback path after retry attempts have failed.

Example:

@Recover
public String recover(Exception ex) {
    return "fallback";
}

text: Which Spring Boot starter is often used to work with Redis caching or messaging?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-data-redis is correct because Redis integration in Boot usually starts with the Redis data starter for repositories, caching, or pub/sub scenarios.

Example:

spring.data.redis.host=localhost

text: Which starter is typically used for MongoDB integration in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb is correct because MongoDB support in Boot is usually added through the MongoDB starter, which wires templates and repository support.

Example:

spring.data.mongodb.uri=mongodb://localhost:27017/appdb

text: Which starter is commonly used to connect Spring Boot with Apache Kafka?
explanation:
spring-kafka is correct because Kafka integration in the Spring ecosystem is commonly provided by the spring-kafka dependency.

Example:

@KafkaListener(topics = "orders")
public void consume(String message) { }

text: Which annotation listens for Kafka messages in a Spring Boot app?
explanation:
@KafkaListener is correct because Use @KafkaListener on a method that should consume messages from a Kafka topic.

Example:

@KafkaListener(topics = "payments")
public void handle(String payload) { }

text: Which starter is commonly used for AMQP and RabbitMQ integration in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring-boot-starter-amqp is correct because Boot’s AMQP starter is the typical entry point for RabbitMQ producers, listeners, and messaging templates.

Example:

@RabbitListener(queues = "email.queue")
public void onMessage(String msg) { }

text: Which annotation is used to listen to RabbitMQ messages in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@RabbitListener is correct because A @RabbitListener method receives messages from a configured queue through Spring AMQP.

Example:

@RabbitListener(queues = "orders.created")
public void receive(String body) { }

text: Which annotation marks a method as transactional in Spring Boot?
explanation:
@Transactional is correct because When several database changes must succeed or fail together, @Transactional creates that transaction boundary.

Example:

@Transactional
public void placeOrder(OrderRequest request) {
    orderRepository.save(...);
    paymentRepository.save(...);
}

text: Which Spring Boot test annotation can inject a TestRestTemplate for real HTTP integration tests?
explanation:
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT) is correct because Running the app on a random port inside a @SpringBootTest lets you exercise endpoints through real HTTP calls.

Example:

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
class ApiTest {
    @Autowired TestRestTemplate restTemplate;
}

text: Which helper client is commonly used in Spring Boot MVC integration tests to call endpoints over HTTP-like semantics?
explanation:
TestRestTemplate is correct because The TestRestTemplate is convenient in Boot integration tests when the app is running on an embedded server.

Example:

ResponseEntity<String> response = restTemplate.getForEntity("/actuator/health", String.class);

text: Which annotation imports additional configuration classes into a Spring Boot test or application context?
explanation:
@Import is correct because Use @Import when a test or configuration class needs extra beans from another configuration class.

Example:

@Import(TestClockConfig.class)
class BillingServiceTest { }

text: Which annotation can override a bean with a Mockito mock in a Spring Boot test?
explanation:
@MockBean is correct because A @MockBean replaces a real bean in the application context, which is very useful when isolating tests.

Example:

@MockBean
private PaymentGateway gateway;

text: Which annotation can wrap a real Spring bean with a Mockito spy in a Spring Boot test?
explanation:
@SpyBean is correct because A @SpyBean keeps real behavior by default while still allowing interaction verification or selective stubbing.

Example:

@SpyBean
private EmailService emailService;

text: Which annotation loads SQL scripts before or after tests in Spring Boot integration testing?
explanation:
@Sql is correct because The @Sql annotation is useful for preparing repeatable database state around test execution.

Example:

@Sql("/test-data.sql")
class CustomerRepositoryTest { }

text: Which property is commonly used to set the application name in Spring Boot?
explanation:
spring.application.name is correct because The application name is often used in logs, tracing, service discovery, and monitoring output.

Example:

spring.application.name=quiz-service

text: Which starter is typically added to generate metadata for configuration properties in IDEs?
explanation:
spring-boot-configuration-processor is correct because The configuration processor helps IDEs understand custom configuration properties and improves autocomplete support.

Example:

<artifactId>spring-boot-configuration-processor</artifactId>

text: Which Spring Boot feature helps avoid writing many explicit version numbers for Spring dependencies?
explanation:
Dependency management is correct because Boot’s curated dependency management keeps versions compatible so you usually omit versions for Spring modules in the build file.

Example:

Example: many starter dependencies do not require a manually specified Spring version.

text: Which annotation is commonly used to declare a bean conditionally when one is missing?
explanation:
@ConditionalOnMissingBean is correct because Auto-configuration often uses @ConditionalOnMissingBean so user-defined beans can override Boot defaults cleanly.

Example:

@Bean
@ConditionalOnMissingBean
Clock clock() {
    return Clock.systemUTC();
}

text: Which annotation is commonly used to create a bean only when a property has a specific value?
explanation:
@ConditionalOnProperty is correct because This condition is useful for feature flags because it enables or disables beans from configuration alone.

Example:

@Bean
@ConditionalOnProperty(name = "feature.audit", havingValue = "true")
AuditService auditService() { ... }

text: Which annotation limits bean creation to web applications only in auto-configuration?
explanation:
@ConditionalOnWebApplication is correct because Boot auto-configuration can adapt to application type, and this condition prevents web-only beans from loading elsewhere.

Example: a servlet filter bean should not load in a non-web batch application.

text: Which annotation creates a bean only when a class is present on the classpath?
explanation:
@ConditionalOnClass is correct because Auto-configuration uses @ConditionalOnClass heavily so optional integrations activate only when their libraries exist.

Example:

@ConditionalOnClass(DataSource.class)
